questions.question: Choose the word most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to "DILIGENT".
questions.solution:
"Diligent" means showing careful and persistent effort in work. "Industrious" (hard-working) is the closest synonym.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Lazy is the opposite of diligent.
(C) Careless is the opposite of diligent (which implies careful effort).
(D) Hesitant relates to indecision, unrelated to diligence.

questions.question: If 'EVIDENCE' is coded as 'FWJEFOEF', then following the identical rule, how is 'WITNESS' coded?
questions.solution: Each letter is shifted forward by +1 in the alphabet: W->X, I->J, T->U, N->O wait, N(+1)=O? Let's check: E(+1)=F, V(+1)=W, I(+1)=J, D(+1)=E, E(+1)=F, N(+1)=O, C(+1)=D? In EVIDENCE (E-V-I-D-E-N-C-E): E->F, V->W, I->J, D->E, E->F, N->O, C->D? Let's use strict +1: W(+1)=X, I(+1)=J, T(+1)=U, N(+1)=O, E(+1)=F, S(+1)=T, S(+1)=T => XJUOFTT.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelled word.
questions.solution:
The correct spelling follows the "i before e except after c" pattern: R-E-C-E-I-V-E.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Reverses the 'ei' to 'ie', which is incorrect after 'c'.
(C) Adds an extra incorrect vowel combination.
(D) Omits the 'i' entirely.

questions.solution:
Each term is double the previous term (a geometric series with ratio 2). 16 × 2 = 32.

questions.question: Two investment funds, Alpha and Beta, yield annual compound returns of 16% and 15% respectively. If an institutional endowment invests ₹10,00,000 divided between the two funds such that both investments yield identical total interest after 2 years (with annual compounding), what is the ratio of capital invested in Fund Alpha to Fund Beta?
questions.solution: Let capital be C1 and C2. Total interest after 2 years is C1 × [(1 + r1)² - 1] = C2 × [(1 + r2)² - 1]. Therefore C1/C2 = [(1 + r2)² - 1] / [(1 + r1)² - 1] = 0.3225 : 0.3456.

questions.question: The average of five numbers is 24. If one number is excluded, the average of the remaining four becomes 22. What is the excluded number?
questions.solution:
Sum of 5 numbers = 5×24 = 120. Sum of remaining 4 numbers = 4×22 = 88. Excluded number = 120 − 88 = 32.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Does not satisfy the given sum condition when checked.
(C) Does not satisfy the given sum condition when checked.
(D) Does not satisfy the given sum condition when checked.

questions.question: A works twice as fast as B. Working together, they complete a task in 6 days. How many days would B alone take to complete the task?
questions.solution:
Let B's rate = 1/x, so A's rate = 2/x. Combined rate = 3/x = 1/6, giving x = 18 days.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Results from an incorrect combined-rate equation.
(C) Results from an incorrect combined-rate equation.
(D) Results from an incorrect combined-rate equation.

questions.question: A person walks 5 km north, then 3 km east, then 5 km south. How far is he from the starting point, and in which direction?
questions.solution:
The 5 km north and 5 km south movements cancel out, leaving only the 3 km eastward displacement. Final position: 3 km east of the start.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Incorrectly adds the north and south distances instead of recognising they cancel out.
(C) Incorrectly retains a residual northward component after the north-south movements cancel.
(D) Uses the wrong distance value instead of the net eastward displacement.

questions.question: A square sheet of paper is folded in half twice (so that it is folded into four layers), and a small triangle is cut from the corner where all the folds meet. When the paper is fully unfolded, how many holes will appear in the sheet?
questions.solution:
Folding twice creates 4 layers of paper at that corner. Cutting through all 4 layers produces 4 separate holes when unfolded.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Corresponds to folding only once (2 layers), not twice.
(C) Would require 8 layers (three folds), not two folds.
(D) Corresponds to no folding at all, i.e., a single layer.
Engineering Mathematics

questions.question: Find d/dx [sin(x²)].
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): By the chain rule, d/dx[sin(u)] = cos(u)·(du/dx) with u = x², du/dx = 2x. So the derivative is 2x·cos(x²).
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Omits the chain-rule factor of 2x from differentiating the inner function x².
(C) Differentiates sin as if it were cos(x²) directly, an incorrect substitution.
(D) Has the correct magnitude but the wrong sign.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫₀⁴ x dx.

• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): ∫x dx = x²/2. Evaluated from 0 to 4: (4²/2) − (0²/2) = 16/2 = 8.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Uses x² directly instead of x²/2, omitting the division by 2 from integration.
(C) Uses only the upper limit value x=4 rather than the definite integral.
(D) Squares the upper limit incorrectly.

questions.question: Water discharges through a sharp-edged orifice of diameter 50 mm under a head of 2 m. Using Cd = 0.62 and Q = Cd·A·√(2gh), calculate the discharge.
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): A = (π/4)(0.05)² = 0.0019635 m². √(2×9.81×2) = √39.24 = 6.264 m/s. Q = 0.62 × 0.0019635 × 6.264 = 0.00762 m³/s = 7.62 L/s.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Uses an incorrect discharge coefficient or area value, overstating the discharge.
(C) Roughly two-thirds of the correct value, from an arithmetic slip.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about tube wells and pumps used in irrigation are CORRECT?

options.A: Specific capacity of a well is defined as the discharge per unit drawdown.
options.B: An increase in drawdown always results in a proportionally equal increase in discharge, regardless of aquifer or well characteristics.
options.C: A submersible pump has its motor coupled directly to the pump, with both installed below the water level.
options.D: The efficiency of a centrifugal pump is generally highest near its rated (design) discharge, known as the best efficiency point (BEP).

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Status of all four options:
(A) [CORRECT] True. Specific capacity is defined precisely as discharge per unit drawdown (Q/s), a standard well-performance parameter.
(B) [INCORRECT] False. Specific capacity typically DECREASES as drawdown/discharge increases, because well losses (which vary with the square of discharge) become proportionally larger — the relationship is not strictly proportional.
(C) [CORRECT] True. This is the standard definition of a submersible pump — motor and pump unit are coupled together and both operate submerged below the water level.
(D) [CORRECT] True. Pump efficiency peaks at the best efficiency point (BEP), which corresponds to the rated/design discharge; efficiency falls off at both lower and higher discharges.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about moisture sorption isotherms of food materials are CORRECT?

options.A: The equilibrium moisture content (EMC) of a hygroscopic material increases with increasing relative humidity of the surrounding air, at constant temperature.
options.B: At a given relative humidity, the EMC obtained during desorption (drying) is generally equal to or greater than that obtained during adsorption (wetting) — a phenomenon known as hysteresis.
options.C: The monolayer moisture value, often estimated using the BET equation, generally represents the moisture content at which a food is most stable against oxidative and microbial deterioration.
options.D: Water activity (aw) is defined as the ratio of the vapour pressure of water in food to the vapour pressure of pure water at the same temperature, and always exceeds 1 for moist foods.

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Status of all four options:
(A) [CORRECT] True. EMC rises with increasing surrounding relative humidity at a given temperature — the defining shape of a sorption isotherm.
(B) [CORRECT] True. Sorption hysteresis is a well-documented phenomenon in which the desorption curve lies above the adsorption curve at the same relative humidity.
(C) [CORRECT] True. The BET monolayer value is widely used as an indicator of the moisture content offering maximum storage stability against oxidation and microbial growth.
(D) [INCORRECT] False. Water activity is defined as p/p₀ (vapour pressure of water in food ÷ vapour pressure of pure water) and by definition ranges from 0 to 1 for foods in equilibrium; it never exceeds 1.

questions.question: Using Bond's law E = 10·Wi·(1/√P80 − 1/√F80), with Wi = 10 kWh/tonne, F80 = 4000 µm, and P80 = 1000 µm, calculate the specific energy required (kWh/tonne). (Round off to two decimal places.)

questions.question: Which of the following statements about thermal processing of foods are CORRECT?

options.A: The z-value represents the temperature change required to change the D-value by a factor of 10.
options.B: Commercial sterilization aims to destroy all pathogenic and toxin-forming organisms, including their spores, under normal storage conditions, though it does not necessarily achieve absolute sterility.
options.C: Blanching before freezing or canning is primarily done to inactivate enzymes that would otherwise cause quality deterioration during storage.
options.D: The F0-value is numerically identical to the D-value of the most heat-resistant spore present in the product, regardless of the actual process time used.

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Status of all four options:
(A) [CORRECT] True. The z-value is defined as the temperature increase needed to reduce the D-value (decimal reduction time) by a factor of 10, characterising the temperature-sensitivity of microbial destruction.
(B) [CORRECT] True. Commercial sterilization targets destruction of pathogens and toxin-formers (and spoilage organisms of concern) under normal storage, while some highly resistant, non-pathogenic spores may still survive — hence it is not absolute sterility.
(C) [CORRECT] True. Blanching is primarily used to inactivate enzymes (e.g., peroxidase, polyphenol oxidase) that would otherwise cause off-flavours, discoloration, and nutrient loss during frozen or canned storage.
(D) [INCORRECT] False. The F0-value depends on the actual time-temperature history of the process (it is the equivalent lethality delivered), not simply on the D-value of the target spore alone — a longer or shorter process changes F0 even for the same organism.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding heat transfer in food processing are CORRECT?

options.A: Thermal diffusivity (α) is defined as α = k/(ρ·cp), where k is thermal conductivity, ρ is density, and cp is specific heat.
options.B: A food product with a higher thermal diffusivity will heat up or cool down FASTER under the same conditions, compared to one with lower thermal diffusivity.
options.C: The convective heat transfer coefficient (h) depends only on the properties of the food product and not on the surrounding fluid flow conditions.
options.D: In canning, the geometric center of the can is generally the "cold point" — the last location to reach the target temperature during conduction-heating.

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Status of all four options:
(A) [CORRECT] True. This is the standard defining equation for thermal diffusivity, combining conductive (k) and storage (ρ·cp) properties into a single rate parameter.
(B) [CORRECT] True. Since thermal diffusivity is a measure of how quickly heat propagates through a material relative to its heat storage, a higher α means faster heating/cooling under identical boundary conditions.
(C) [INCORRECT] False. The convective heat transfer coefficient depends strongly on the surrounding fluid flow conditions (velocity, turbulence, fluid properties), not solely on the food product's own properties.
(D) [CORRECT] True. For conduction-heated canned products, the geometric center is the point furthest from all surfaces and therefore heats up last, making it the standard 'cold point' used for process design.
